findings.title: Client removal throws when V1 and V2 features are both enabled
findings.body: The listener runs when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) is enabled. `management()` returns the V2 implementation whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled (lines 40-67). V2 does not depend on V1 (Profile.java:58). With both features on, a `ClientRemovedEvent` now calls `ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled`, which throws `UnsupportedOperationException` (ClientPermissionsV2.java:193). That breaks client deletion. The new gate does not prevent this, because both features are on in that case. With V2 only, the gate skips the role, client and group cleanup entirely. Choose the branch by whether V2 is active. Skip the client cleanup, or make V2 `setPermissionsEnabled` a no-op, when V2 is active.

findings.title: Dead code and unused imports
findings.body: The private `getEvaluationContext` is never called. The imports for `TOKEN_EXCHANGE`, `Logger` (the `logger` field is unused), `ClientModelIdentity`, `DefaultEvaluationContext` and `EvaluationContext` exist only for that dead code or for nothing. Remove them. The two `hasPermission` overloads and `hasGrantedPermission` also duplicate the scope-matching loop.

findings.title: Mixes JUnit 4 `fail` into a JUnit 5 test
findings.body: `org.junit.Assert.fail` is imported while the rest of the class uses `org.junit.jupiter`. Use `org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.fail`. Also, `fail(...)` throws an `AssertionError`, which the surrounding `catch (Exception)` does not catch, so this works. `assertThrows(ForbiddenException.class, ...)` would be clearer.

contracts.action: Test calls now pass the injected client to the static helpers getScopePermissionsResource(client) and createPermission(client, permission)
contracts.equivalent_path: The old instance helpers in AbstractPermissionTest, which used the injected admin-permissions client field.
contracts.before_after: The static helpers take a ManagedClient and call client.admin().authorization().permissions().scope(). Every call site passes the same injected `client` field, so the target is unchanged.
contracts.failure_mode: None found. No call site was missed, and the file has no leftover zero-arg calls.

summary:
**Batch 1 of 2.** The V2 client permission evaluator looks sound. The main risk is the AdminPermissions event listener. It now runs only when V1 is enabled, but V2 `setPermissionsEnabled` throws, so deleting a client fails when both features are on. With V2 only, the cleanup is skipped. I also found dead code in ClientPermissionsV2 and a JUnit 4 import in a JUnit 5 test. I only read the code and did not run any tests.

**Batch 2 of 2.** I found nothing to flag in UserResourceTypePermissionTest. The change only moves the test to the new static helpers `getScopePermissionsResource(client)` and `createPermission(client, ...)`. Every call site passes the same injected `client`, so behaviour is unchanged. I read the whole file and the helper signatures in AbstractPermissionTest.
